B. Broom bristles scratch the glaze off bisque-fired pottery sitting on drying shelves.
C. Dry clay dust reacts with room humidity to make the potter's wheel motor overheat.
D. Wet mopping is the only way to dissolve lead oxide out of raw earthenware clay bodies.

pamphlet_excerpts: Counselor's Approval Do ONE: Your Parent or Guardian's Permission: Because many high-fire kilns are built by individuals, each kiln follows a unique schedule (p. 25).
Counselor's Approval Do ONE Principle 2: Your Parent or Guardian's Permission Principle 2: Do not attempt to fire any fuel-burning kiln without close supervision from the owner (p. 25).

Counselor's Approval Do ONE Principle 3: Your Parent or Guardian's Permission Principle 3: Copper oxide can produce a brilliantred in a reduction firing, but it would produce greens inan oxidation firing (p. 25).
Counselor's Approval Do ONE Principle 4: Your Parent or Guardian's Permission Principle 4: Fuel must have a sufficient amount of oxygen to burn (p. 25).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Counselor's Approval Do ONE): Step 1 (Your Parent or Guardian's Permission): The dampers in fuel-burning kilns enable the potter to adjust the amount of oxygen inside the kiln (p. 25).

Step 2 (Counselor's Approval Do ONE): Step 2 (Your Parent or Guardian's Permission): When the kiln contains more than enough oxygen needed to completely burn the amount of fuel being used, the atmosphere inside the kiln is oxidized (p. 25).

Step 3 (Counselor's Approval Do ONE): Step 3 (Your Parent or Guardian's Permission): In a reduction firing, the flame is seeking oxygen inside the kiln, and because there isn't enough, it "steals" oxygen from the clay and glazes (p. 25).
Step 4 (Counselor's Approval Do ONE): Step 4 (Your Parent or Guardian's Permission): This chemical reaction darkens the clay and changes the look and texture of some glazes (p. 25).

options: A. Dry sweeping launches fine crystalline silica dust into the air, which can cause permanent lung damage (silicosis) when inhaled over time.
B. Broom bristles scratch the glaze off bisque-fired pottery sitting on drying shelves.
C. Dry clay dust reacts with room humidity to make the potter's wheel motor overheat.
D. Wet mopping is the only way to dissolve lead oxide out of raw earthenware clay bodies.
choices: A. Dry sweeping launches fine crystalline silica dust into the air, which can cause permanent lung damage (silicosis) when inhaled over time.
B. Broom bristles scratch the glaze off bisque-fired pottery sitting on drying shelves.
C. Dry clay dust reacts with room humidity to make the potter's wheel motor overheat.

patrol_quiz_bank.correct_answer: A. Dry sweeping launches fine crystalline silica dust into the air, which can cause permanent lung damage (silicosis) when inhaled over time.
patrol_quiz_bank.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Clay and glaze powders contain fine silica particles that stay suspended in the air when dry-swept; wiping surfaces and mopping floors with water traps dust safely.
